original.target_description: MIE Recognition Test: overall recognition accuracy for high-reward versus low-reward scenes, 20–26 hours after scanning; paired within-subject comparison, one-tailed.

es.location: p. 509, Behavioral Results, MIE Recognition Test
es.quote: As expected, recognition accuracy ... was greater for high-reward than low-reward scenes ... [t(11) = 2.14, p = 0.03, one-tailed].

notes: Identity independently confirmed from supplied source header: Reward-Motivated Learning: Mesolimbic Activation Precedes Memory Formation; R. Alison Adcock, Arul Thangavel, Susan Whitfield-Gabrieli, Brian Knutson, and John D.E. Gabrieli; Neuron 50, 507–517, May 4, 2006; DOI 10.1016/j.neuron.2006.03.036. Supplied text is a full primary research article with Results, Experimental Procedures, and References, not an abstract or secondary report. No PDF was supplied. Only es_value_o is assigned; all other fields/sides are null placeholders, not absence findings. Target maps by outcome to overall scene recognition accuracy, explicitly high-reward versus low-reward; printed t(11) = 2.14, same-test p = 0.03, one-tailed. The section separately reports t(11) = 2.59, p = 0.02, two-tailed for correct high-confidence responses (Remember and Know pooled); this restricted outcome is distinct from overall scene recognition. High- and low-value versus false-alarm comparisons are also distinct tests. No statistic conversion or N derivation performed.
